newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch mull massive pig cull -- TV report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch mull massive pig cull -- TV report.

text.p: The Dutch Farm Ministry declined on Wednesday to comment on a news report that it was planning to cull around a million pigs at 1,600 farms to snuff out the swine fever epidemic in the south of the Netherlands.
"We have absolutely no comment to make," a spokesman for the ministry told Reuters.
Dutch television said Farm Minister Jozias van Aartsen had asked the Dutch Defence Ministry to draw up a plan to kill the animals, which it said the ministry was considering.

The Farm Ministry spokesman confirmed there had been a general request for help to the Defence Ministry and said Van Aartsen would send a letter to parliament on Thursday but declined to elaborate on its contents.
It said that so far some 650,000 pigs had been destroyed in attempts to contain the highly contagious disease. It declined to say whether a further million pigs needed to be killed.

The latest swine fever outbreak, the first in the Netherlands since 1992, broke out in February, and since then many of the country's trading partners including the United States have banned imports of Dutch pigs and pork products.
Last year the Netherlands -- which has some 14 million pigs -- exported almost a million tonnes of pigs and products, bringing in around 5.1 billion guilders.
